01-observer-gap.question: If an isolated apparatus evolves linearly with a qubit via \(U\ket{0,A_r}=\ket{0,A_0}\) and \(U\ket{1,A_r}=\ket{1,A_1}\), what state results from input \((\ket{0}+i\ket{1})/\sqrt{2} \otimes \ket{A_r}\)?
hints: Apply linearity of \(U\) to each basis term.
01-observer-gap.answer: The joint state becomes \((\ket{0,A_0} + i\ket{1,A_1})/\sqrt{2}\), an entangled superposition of system and apparatus.

01-observer-gap.question: Suppose Alice claims she can send a bit to Bob faster than light by choosing whether to consciously observe her half of a Bell pair \(\ket{\Phi^+}\). Why does this fail?
hints: Compute Bob's reduced density matrix \(\rho_B = \operatorname{Tr}_A(\ketbra{\Phi^+}{\Phi^+})\) before and after Alice's local action.
01-observer-gap.answer: Regardless of whether Alice applies a local unitary, measures, or observes, Bob's marginal state remains \(I/2\). No local statistics at Bob's lab change without classical communication.

01-observer-gap.question: Give an example of a physical system that forms a stable record without intelligence, and an intelligent system that lacks obvious signs of consciousness.
hints: Think of a photographic plate or crystal defect, and of a specialized optimization algorithm.
01-observer-gap.answer: A particle track in a cloud chamber or photographic emulsion is a physical record with no intelligence. A stateless chess engine or gradient-descent optimizer exhibits goal-directed intelligence without persistent self-modeling or phenomenal unity.

02-subsystems-decoherence.question: A qubit in \(\alpha\ket{0}+\beta\ket{1}\) interacts with \(N\) environment qubits initially in \(\ket{0}^{\otimes N}\) via CNOTs, giving \(\alpha\ket{0}\ket{0}^{\otimes N} + \beta\ket{1}\ket{1}^{\otimes N}\). Compute the reduced density matrix \(\rho_S\).
hints: Trace out all \(N\) environment qubits; notice \(\braket{0^{\otimes N}|1^{\otimes N}} = 0\).
02-subsystems-decoherence.answer: \(\rho_S = |\alpha|^2\ketbra{0}{0} + |\beta|^2\ketbra{1}{1}\). All off-diagonal coherence terms vanish locally once the environment states are orthogonal.

02-subsystems-decoherence.question: Why are eigenstates of the interaction Hamiltonian's system coupling operator \(H_{\text{int}} = S \otimes E\) natural pointer states?
hints: Check whether \(S\) commutes with projections onto those states.
02-subsystems-decoherence.answer: States \(\ket{s_i}\) satisfying \(S\ket{s_i} = s_i\ket{s_i}\) do not become entangled with \(E\) under \(\exp(-i H_{\text{int}} t/\hbar)\); they merely induce environment-conditional phases and remain unentangled.

02-subsystems-decoherence.question: In Quantum Darwinism, why is redundancy \(R_\delta\) across small environmental fragments essential for objectivity?
hints: Consider what happens if all information about \(S\) sits in one global entangled mode.
02-subsystems-decoherence.answer: If information is encoded only globally, a single observer capturing a small fragment learns nothing. When many disjoint fragments each carry near-complete classical information about the pointer observable, multiple observers agree independently.

03-memory-entropy.question: A memory qubit starts in the maximally mixed state \(\rho_M = I/2\). What is its von Neumann entropy in bits, and what happens to its entropy when it is reset to \(\ket{0}\)?
hints: Use \(S(\rho) = -\operatorname{Tr}(\rho \log_2 \rho)\).
03-memory-entropy.answer: Its initial entropy is \(S(I/2) = 1\) bit. Resetting it to the pure state \(\ket{0}\) reduces its entropy to \(0\) bits, so at least 1 bit of entropy must be exported to the environment.

03-memory-entropy.question: At room temperature \(T = 300\,\text{K}\) (with \(k_B \approx 1.38\times 10^{-23}\,\text{J/K}\)), estimate the Landauer minimum heat \(Q_{\min} = k_B T \ln 2\) dissipated by erasing one bit.
hints: Multiply \(1.38\times 10^{-23} \times 300 \times 0.693\).
03-memory-entropy.answer: \(Q_{\min} \approx 2.87 \times 10^{-21}\,\text{J}\). Modern CMOS transistors dissipate orders of magnitude more, though nanoscale experiments approach this bound.

03-memory-entropy.question: Does a reversible CNOT gate that copies a classical bit \(\ket{x}\ket{0} \to \ket{x}\ket{x}\) require \(k_B T \ln 2\) of heat dissipation?
hints: Check whether the target register started in a known pure state \(\ket{0}\) or an unknown mixed state.
03-memory-entropy.answer: No. Copying into a clean, pre-initialized register \(\ket{0}\) is logically and thermodynamically reversible. The Landauer cost arises only when an unknown memory state is erased or overwritten to prepare \(\ket{0}\) in the first place.

04-defining-intelligence.question: In an agent–environment decomposition \(\mathcal{H}_A \otimes \mathcal{H}_E\), why is a sensor channel never a purely unitary gate on \(\mathcal{H}_A\) alone?
hints: An agent's internal state must become correlated with external states in \(\mathcal{H}_E\).
04-defining-intelligence.answer: A unitary acting solely on \(\mathcal{H}_A\) cannot depend on \(\mathcal{H}_E\). Sensing requires an interaction coupling \(\mathcal{H}_E\) to \(\mathcal{H}_A\), which appears locally on \(\mathcal{H}_A\) as an environment-conditioned channel.

04-defining-intelligence.question: Suppose an agent maintains a model distribution \(q(x)\) for an environmental state with true distribution \(p(x)\). Show why minimizing the Kullback–Leibler divergence \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q)\) is equivalent to minimizing expected log-loss (surprise).
hints: Expand \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q) = \sum_x p(x)\log(p(x)/q(x))\).
04-defining-intelligence.answer: \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(p\|q) = -H(p) - \sum_x p(x)\log q(x)\). Since the true entropy \(H(p)\) is fixed with respect to the agent's model \(q\), minimizing \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}\) minimizes the expected surprise \(-\sum_x p(x)\log q(x)\).

04-defining-intelligence.question: Under our physical definition of intelligence, why must memory compression and thermodynamic cost appear alongside prediction accuracy?
hints: Think of a lookup table that memorizes every past event without generalizing or fitting inside finite energy.
04-defining-intelligence.answer: An infinitely large lookup table could store past observations without generalizing, but any physical agent has finite Hilbert-space/memory capacity and finite free energy. Intelligence requires extracting predictive structure efficiently within those bounds.

05-quantum-limits-intelligence.question: An agent wants to learn whether a qubit was prepared in \(\ket{0}\) or \(\ket{+}\), each with prior probability \(1/2\). What is the maximum probability of guessing correctly (Helstrom bound)?
hints: Use \(P_{\text{succ}} = \frac{1}{2}\bigl(1 + \frac{1}{2}\|\rho_0 - \rho_1\|_1\bigr)\) with \(|\braket{0|+}| = 1/\sqrt{2}\).

05-quantum-limits-intelligence.question: Why does Holevo's bound prevent an agent from storing and reading out 100 independent classical bits from a single qubit?
hints: Compare the Hilbert space dimension of one qubit with \(\chi \le S(\rho) \le \log_2 d\).
05-quantum-limits-intelligence.answer: For a qubit, \(d=2\), so the von Neumann entropy \(S(\rho) \le 1\) bit. Holevo's bound guarantees that at most 1 bit of mutual information can be retrieved by any measurement.

05-quantum-limits-intelligence.question: Name one setting where a quantum sensor or quantum agent strictly outperforms any classical agent with the same number of probes.
hints: Consider phase estimation across \(N\) entangled probes (Heisenberg limit) or Grover-like unstructured search.
05-quantum-limits-intelligence.answer: Using an \(N\)-qubit GHZ probe state achieves phase-estimation precision scaling as \(1/N\) (Heisenberg limit) rather than the classical \(1/\sqrt{N}\) shot-noise limit.

06-quantum-observers.question: Why can we shift the Heisenberg cut from between (system, detector) to between (system+detector, environment) without changing predictions for final macroscopic records?
hints: Both cuts apply the Born rule after the unitary correlation has formed.
06-quantum-observers.answer: Because unitary premeasurement transfers the relevant amplitudes faithfully into the detector basis, applying the Born rule before or after the apparatus coupling yields identical outcome probabilities.

06-quantum-observers.question: In Wigner's friend, the friend measures \((\ket{0}+\ket{1})/\sqrt{2}\) inside a sealed lab, yielding \((\ket{0,F_0}+\ket{1,F_1})/\sqrt{2}\). If Wigner performs an interference measurement in the basis \(|\pm_L\rangle = (\ket{0,F_0}\pm\ket{1,F_1})/\sqrt{2}\), what are the probabilities?
hints: Compute \(|\braket{+_L|\Psi}|^2\).
06-quantum-observers.answer: Wigner obtains \(|+_L\rangle\) with probability 1 and \(|-_L\rangle\) with probability 0—demonstrating that coherent superpositions of the friend's memory remain physically distinguishable to a superobserver.

06-quantum-observers.question: Why does Breuer's self-reference theorem prevent a physical observer from completely measuring its own total quantum state from within?
hints: No apparatus can distinguish all states of a composite system that includes the apparatus itself.
06-quantum-observers.answer: A system cannot contain a subsystem with strictly more orthogonal record states than the total system possesses; an internal observer's readout map is necessarily non-injective on states of the full observer+world.

07-intelligence-vs-consciousness.question: Explain why passing a behavioral Turing-style test establishes functional intelligence rather than consciousness.
hints: Compare external input-output maps with internal dynamical structure.
07-intelligence-vs-consciousness.answer: Many distinct internal physical architectures—including a giant unintegrated lookup table or a stateless feedforward network—can realize the same input-output function without unified intrinsic dynamics or self-monitoring.

07-intelligence-vs-consciousness.question: Suppose two non-interacting computers run side by side inside one chassis, each processing half of a video stream without exchanging signals. Why do they fail the physical binding condition?
hints: Check whether the joint state or dynamics factorizes across the partition.
07-intelligence-vs-consciousness.answer: Their joint state and evolution factorize cleanly as \(\rho_1 \otimes \rho_2\) and \(U_1 \otimes U_2\). There is no integrated whole beyond two independent subsystems.

07-intelligence-vs-consciousness.question: In what sense is first-person perspective compatible with a universal third-person density operator \(\rho\)?
hints: Think of conditional states and intrinsic subsystem decompositions.
07-intelligence-vs-consciousness.answer: A global third-person description specifies correlations across subsystems; a first-person perspective corresponds to the intrinsic, conditional information structure available to a particular integrated subsystem across its own internal boundary.

08-quantum-constraints-consciousness.question: If thermal collisions in warm brain tissue scatter off a spatial superposition separated by \(\Delta x \sim 10^{-9}\,\text{m}\) at a rate producing decoherence in \(\tau_D \sim 10^{-13}\,\text{s}\), compare \(\tau_D\) with a typical neural firing timescale \(\tau_{\text{neural}} \sim 10^{-3}\,\text{s}\).
hints: Take the ratio \(\tau_{\text{neural}}/\tau_D\).
08-quantum-constraints-consciousness.answer: \(\tau_{\text{neural}}/\tau_D \sim 10^{10}\). Without active quantum error correction or an unusually shielded degree of freedom, coherent spatial superpositions decohere ten billion times faster than a single neural spike.

08-quantum-constraints-consciousness.question: How do objective-collapse models differ experimentally from standard unitary quantum mechanics plus decoherence?
hints: Look for energy non-conservation, spontaneous heating/radiation, or loss of matter-wave interference.
08-quantum-constraints-consciousness.answer: Collapse models modify the Schrödinger equation with stochastic nonlinear terms, predicting spontaneous momentum diffusion (anomalous heating/X-ray emission) and interference loss even in perfectly isolated systems.

08-quantum-constraints-consciousness.question: For a two-qubit Bell state \(\ket{\Phi^+}\), compute the minimum mutual information or trace-distance divergence between \(\rho_{AB}\) and the product of its marginals \(\rho_A \otimes \rho_B\).
hints: Use quantum mutual information \(I(A:B) = S(\rho_A) + S(\rho_B) - S(\rho_{AB})\).
08-quantum-constraints-consciousness.answer: \(S(\rho_A) = 1\), \(S(\rho_B) = 1\), and \(S(\rho_{AB}) = 0\), so \(I(A:B) = 2\) bits. The state cannot be factored into independent parts across the \(A|B\) cut.

09-defining-consciousness.question: Why are all three pillars—integration across cuts, autonomous boundary maintenance, and reflexive self-modeling—needed to avoid classifying a Bell pair or a thermostat as conscious?
hints: Test a Bell pair against self-modeling and a thermostat against integration.
09-defining-consciousness.answer: A Bell pair is maximally non-factorizable (high integration) but lacks autonomous thermodynamic boundary maintenance and an internal self-world model. A simple thermostat maintains a target variable but lacks high-dimensional integrated self-modeling.

09-defining-consciousness.question: In our formal definition, why does consciousness live at the level of coarse-grained pointer dynamics rather than bare microscopic particle coordinates?
hints: Compare microscopic thermal fluctuations with stable macroscopic/mesoscopic records.
09-defining-consciousness.answer: Microscopic degrees of freedom thermalize and decohere continuously; only coarse-grained pointer subspaces preserve stable information long enough to support integrated memory and self-modeling.

09-defining-consciousness.question: Does defining a conscious subsystem inside an open quantum system require consciousness to cause wavefunction collapse?
hints: Check whether the definition modifies the Schrödinger equation or the Born rule.
09-defining-consciousness.answer: No. The definition characterizes a structural and dynamical organization within standard unitary + open-system quantum mechanics. It neither adds a collapse postulate nor alters any physical transition probability.

10-minds-machines-quantum-agents.question: Under our definitions, how can a biological brain be conscious if its neurons operate in a decohered, effectively classical pointer regime?
hints: Check whether classical pointer dynamics can still satisfy dynamical irreducibility, autonomy, and reflexive self-modeling.
10-minds-machines-quantum-agents.answer: Quantum compatibility does not require macroscopic entanglement across the whole brain. A dissipative biological network running on stabilized pointer states can still form an irreducible, self-modeling dynamical system inside quantum theory.

10-minds-machines-quantum-agents.question: Why does a stateless transformer language model satisfy much of the functional definition of intelligence during inference while failing the definition of consciousness?
hints: Check persistent autonomous boundary maintenance and continuous reflexive self-modeling.
10-minds-machines-quantum-agents.answer: Between tokens, it has no persistent autonomous self-boundary, no continuous thermodynamic self-maintenance, and no unified internal dynamical loop integrating an ongoing self-model across time.

10-minds-machines-quantum-agents.question: What would distinguish a genuinely quantum-coherent agent from a classical-pointer conscious system in future experiments?
hints: Think of coherent quantum memory, Wigner's-friend-style interference tests, or entanglement-assisted integration.
10-minds-machines-quantum-agents.answer: A quantum-coherent agent could maintain coherent superpositions of internal model branches across decision cycles and exhibit quantum-enhanced integration (\(I(A:B) > \log d\) via entanglement) testable through interferometric or Bell-like protocols.
